blocks.text: Moody Park Houses: streets and boundaries

items.t: The park at the centre is the boundary anchor: Moody Park covers 9.62 hectares, bounded by Eighth Avenue north, Eighth Street east, Sixth Avenue south and Tenth Street west.
The neighbourhood takes the park's name, and the park was envisioned in 1863 as Moody Square, named for Colonel Richard Clement Moody.

blocks.text: Moody Park Houses: the housing stock

items.t: Houses here are early stock: residential construction along Sixth Avenue began shortly after the park was cleared in 1889, and the neighbourhood was largely developed and serviced by streetcar by the First World War.
A dated example survives at 1013 Sixth Avenue, a two-storey front-gabled house built between 1892 and 1902, on the Community Heritage Register since April 27, 2009.

blocks.text: Moody Park Houses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The park doubles as a tree collection: its mature specimen trees, including Douglas fir, western red cedar and Oregon white oak, make it function like an arboretum, and its diagonal paths follow landscape architect R.H. Savery's 1936 plan.
An outdoor fitness circuit sits between Century House and the soccer field, with an accessible stationary hand bike among its stations.
Moody Park is one of seven New Westminster parks where adults 19 and over may drink in designated areas, between 11:00 a.m. and dusk only.
The park's lacrosse box and outdoor stage were listed as closed for construction on the City's community parks page when read.

blocks.text: Moody Park Houses: development and new projects

items.t: The newest civic building touching this area is already built: the təməsew̓txʷ Aquatic and Community Centre at 65 East Sixth Avenue replaced Canada Games Pool and the Centennial Community Centre — status: completed facility (as of November 3, 2026).
The nearest SkyTrain access is at the area's west side: TransLink's system map shows 22nd Street Station on the Expo Line in New Westminster, on the line toward Waterfront and Surrey.

blocks.text: Moody Park Houses: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check heritage status first: look up the address on the City of New Westminster Heritage Register before assuming a teardown or exterior change is permitted, because register recognition is recorded house by house, as at 1013 Sixth Avenue.
The register entry states what is significant about a listed house; it does not tell a buyer what a specific renovation will be approved — that is a City permit decision.

faq.a: Moody Park holds the neighbourhood's main outdoor recreation in one block. The City lists an outdoor pool at 701 Tenth Street, three tennis courts shared with three pickleball courts, a full and a half basketball court, and a 2,430-square-metre off-leash dog area added in August 2015 with three gated entrances. Its spray park is currently closed and listed as reopening in summer 2027.
faq.q: What is inside Moody Park itself?

faq.a: Century House is the City's membership centre for adults aged 50 and over, beside Moody Park. The City states annual membership is $25 and covers social and activity clubs, fitness, education, counselling and peer support, with trained senior volunteers providing one-to-one peer support at no cost. It is a seniors' activity centre, not a care home or a housing complex.

The City states the name is the hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓ word for “sea otter house,” chosen by a Naming Advisory Panel of local First Nations and urban Indigenous representatives, and that the facility replaced Canada Games Pool and the Centennial Community Centre.
faq.q: What replaced the Canada Games Pool?

faq.a: Two School District No. 40 (New Westminster) elementaries are in the wider pocket: Lord Kelvin Elementary, kindergarten to Grade 5, at 1010 Hamilton Street, and Lord Tweedsmuir Elementary, kindergarten to Grade 5, at 1714 Eighth Avenue. 40 assigns by home address, so confirm the catchment for the specific house before relying on either school.
